$schema-note: Read tests/temp-dirs-outside-the-repo.test.ts first. Both sets are RATCHETS over a measured population, not licences: the guard asserts them in BOTH directions, so an entry whose file has stopped offending reds the guard until the entry is deleted. The write set pins a MULTISET of licensed destinations — pinning only the count let three legitimate fixture writes be SUBSTITUTED for three `tests/*.tmp.ts` writes, and pinning only the destinations let a licensed write be DUPLICATED, both with the guard still green. The leak set pins counts per file, so a new leak inside an already-listed file reds too.

packages/kn-next/src/__tests__/adapter-d.reason: Boots a REAL `next dev` server against a checked-in fixture project, so these three destinations — the generated `.knext/adapter.mjs` bundle, its `.gitignore`, and the `node_modules/@types` symlink parent — have to sit inside that project. Next resolves a project by directory, and a dev server rooted at a temp copy would no longer be exercising the tracked fixture the test names. Not the #918 shape either: nothing here writes a transient `.ts` into `tests/`, which is what raced the typecheck gate. The licence is these three EXPRESSIONS: any other destination in this file, including one substituted for one of these, is a red.

unremovedTempDirs.note: 161 unremoved `mkdtemp` sites across 48 files, measured when the LIFETIME half of this guard landed (D9). Burn-down tracked in #939 — note the sizing there: 161/48, not the 156/49 the issue was filed with, because two rounds of review found the scan crediting cleanups it should not have (one `rmSync` for many same-named creations; a registry push discharging unenrolled siblings; removing a FILE INSIDE a directory counted as removing the directory). They are recorded rather than fixed because fixing them means touching 48 files across every package mid-sprint, and a guard that lands with its subject already red teaches people to disable it. This list is a CEILING: a file may only leak fewer than it does today, never more, and a file that stops leaking must leave the list. Nothing may be added to it — a new leak is a red, including a new leak in a file already here and a new leak that reuses a binding name already here. That last clause was FALSE when it was first written: twelve file/name pairs had a leak name colliding with a drained registry's loop element, whose own `rmSync(d)` was being counted a second time as a direct removal, so a leak under that one name would have ridden free. Credit inside a drain body is now counted per enrolment only, and the guard proves the claim on the colliding name rather than on a name chosen to pass.
